interview.note: Sample guides. The avatar is a mock: no Synthesia connection exists yet. In the Werkbank app the task check, the summary and the letter text come from Joule (an AI). Without the app, or if the AI is not reachable, a text search stands in for the check and says so. It never decides about a person.

notice.title: Before we start: you will talk to an AI avatar
points: You are speaking with an AI avatar, not with a person. The questions come from a guide the hiring manager approved.
Your answers are written down as text so the hiring manager can read them. Do not share health, family or other personal data.

Your task result is checked by an AI against the criteria listed with the task. The check says correct, partly correct, wrong or not present for each criterion. It gives no score and rejects nobody. You see the result too.

To do this, your answers and your task text are sent to an AI model provider (OpenRouter, through Joule). The hiring manager keeps a record of answers, task text, result and a short summary. It holds no name and no e-mail address; a session code stands for you.
If you want a letter with the summary and your result, you type an e-mail address for that. It is used to create a mail draft and is not stored. A person sends the mail.
A person, the hiring manager, makes every decision about your application. You can ask for a conversation with a person instead at any time.

REQ-2203.intro: Welcome. I will ask a few questions about your work with data and then give you a short SQL task.

questions.text: Tell me about an analysis you did that changed a decision in supply chain or planning.

What data was used and how

questions.text: Explain a forecast error to a warehouse manager who does not work with statistics.

task.title: Late deliveries per supplier
task.brief: Table deliveries(supplier_id, order_id, promised_date, delivered_date). Write a query that returns, for each supplier, the number of deliveries that arrived after the promised date in 2026, only for suppliers with at least 3 late deliveries, sorted by that number, highest first.

criteria.text: Counts late deliveries per supplier (GROUP BY supplier)
Keeps suppliers with at least 3 late deliveries (HAVING)

task.sample:
SELECT supplier_id, COUNT(*) AS late_count
FROM deliveries
WHERE delivered_date > promised_date
  AND delivered_date >= '2026-01-01' AND delivered_date < '2027-01-01'
GROUP BY supplier_id
HAVING COUNT(*) >= 3
ORDER BY late_count DESC;

task.title: Shift plan with two absences
task.brief: Your shift has 12 people. Two forklift drivers are sick. Four trucks arrive between 06:00 and 08:00, two of them with fresh goods. Write down how you re-plan the first two hours: who does what, what you move back, and whom you inform.

criteria.text: Puts the fresh goods trucks first
Covers the missing forklift drivers (licensed staff only)

task.sample: I put the fresh goods trucks first at 06:00. Only licensed drivers take the forklifts, so I move the two best-placed licensed people there. The dry goods truck is pushed back to after 07:00. I inform transport planning about the delay.

task.brief: Payroll cost for the Hamburg site is 18% higher than last month. Before release you must find out why. Write the checks you would run, in order, and when you would stop the release.

rubric.note: Five levels per dimension, read from the written answers only. Equal weights. The AI proposes, the hiring manager sets the final level.

dimensions.label: Content
dimensions.asks: How concrete, correct and deep is what the person says?

anchors.1: No concrete case or fact; answers stay general or miss the question.
anchors.2: Names topics, but without an own example or a reason.
anchors.3: One or two concrete examples; the basics are correct; reasons are partly given.
anchors.4: Several concrete examples with own role, method and result; reasons are given.
anchors.5: Precise, deep and correct throughout; weighs trade-offs and knows the limits of the own approach.

dimensions.label: Collaboration & reflection
dimensions.asks: What do the examples show about working with others and learning from mistakes?

anchors.1: No example of working with others or of learning from a mistake.
anchors.2: Mentions others or a mistake, but vaguely or by blaming.
anchors.3: Describes working with others and one lesson learned, in general terms.
anchors.4: Concrete examples of handling disagreement and of changing the own mind; names the own part.
anchors.5: Takes ownership, shows how others were brought along and what changed afterwards.

dimensions.label: Rhetoric
dimensions.asks: How well is the answer built and fitted to the listener? Structure and clarity only, not spelling, grammar or language level.

anchors.1: Hard to follow; no structure; the question is not answered.
anchors.2: An answer is there but scattered; the point comes late or not at all.
anchors.3: A clear main point and some structure; partly fitted to the listener.
anchors.4: Point first, then reasons; fitted to the listener; plain words.
anchors.5: Compact, vivid and fitted to the listener; keeps the thread when challenged.

dimensions.label: Creativity
dimensions.asks: How many different ideas are there, and how well are they argued?

anchors.1: No own idea; repeats the question or a standard answer.
anchors.2: One standard idea without a reason.
anchors.3: Two ideas, or one fresh idea, with a reason.
anchors.4: Several clearly different ideas, with trade-offs.
anchors.5: Original ideas that reframe the problem, with a way to test them.

first.note: First interview with a live AI avatar (Mira). Questions and the facts she may use are approved by the hiring manager. She answers questions about the company only from the approved facts and says so when she does not know. The conversation is written down as text; no audio is kept. Fictional company.

notice.title: Before we start: a conversation with an AI avatar
points: You are talking to an AI avatar, not to a person. The avatar asks questions that the hiring manager approved and can answer questions about the company and the next steps.
The conversation is recorded as text, word by word, with times. No audio and no video are kept. The hiring manager reads the text. Do not share health, family or other personal data.
If you speak, your voice goes from the app to a speech service that turns it into text, and the text goes to an AI model provider (OpenRouter, through Joule). You can type instead.
The avatar answers questions about the company only from facts the hiring manager approved. If it does not know, it says so and notes your question for a person.
The avatar does not rate you and does not decide. A person, the hiring manager, decides about every application. You can ask for a conversation with a person at any time.

process.text: This conversation. The hiring manager reads the written record.
A conversation with the team on site, about 60 minutes. You meet the people you would work with.
A short talk with the head of the department about open questions and the start date.
If everything fits, you get an offer from a person in HR.

shared.text: Hanse Logistik is a fictional logistics company with sites in Hamburg, Bremen and Köln. It moves goods for retail and industry customers by road and rail and runs its own warehouses.
About 2,400 people work for Hanse Logistik, around 900 of them in Hamburg.
Safety comes first at every site. Teams decide close to the work, and mistakes are talked about openly instead of hidden.

Office roles work 38 hours a week with flexible start times. Warehouse roles work in shifts that are published four weeks ahead. Part-time is possible for most roles; ask the hiring manager for this job.
30 days of holiday, a company pension plan, and a yearly training budget. Details are in the offer, which a person prepares.
I cannot name pay. The pay range for the job is in the job posting, and the hiring manager talks about it with you in person.

After this conversation the hiring manager reads the written record. You hear from a person within about 7 days. Then come an in-person interview, a final conversation and, if everything fits, an offer.
The conversation is kept as text for the hiring manager. No audio and no video are kept. It holds no name and no e-mail address; a session code stands for you. You can ask a person to delete it.

REQ-2201.intro: Welcome. I would like to learn how you lead a team on a shift. Then you can ask me anything about Hanse Logistik and the next steps.

questions.text: What draws you to leading a shift, and why at a logistics company?
Tell me about a time you had to get a team moving when it was under pressure. What did you do?
How do you make sure safety rules are followed when time is short?
Which shifts could you work, and when could you start?

knowledge.text: The Warehouse Shift Lead in Hamburg leads a shift of about 12 people, plans who works at which gate, and is the contact for drivers and the transport planners.
You report to the Head of Operations Hamburg. The shift team has forklift drivers, pickers and a deputy.
The warehouse runs early, late and night shifts. Shift plans are published four weeks ahead, and weekends are shared in a rota.
A forklift licence is helpful. Hanse Logistik pays for missing licences and for a leadership course in the first year.

REQ-2203.intro: Welcome. I would like to hear about your work with data. Then you can ask me anything about Hanse Logistik and the next steps.

questions.text: What draws you to supply chain analysis, and why at Hanse Logistik?
Tell me about an analysis you did that changed a decision. What was the data and what changed?
How do you check that a number is right before you share it?
Which tools do you use for analysis, and when could you start?

knowledge.text: The Supply Chain Analyst in Hamburg builds reports and forecasts on transport and warehouse data and helps planners decide where to add capacity.
The analyst works in the planning team in Hamburg with four planners and one data engineer.
The team works mainly with SQL and Excel, and uses SAP data. Python is welcome but not required.
The role is hybrid: about two days a week at home, three in the Hamburg office.

REQ-2206.intro: Welcome. I would like to learn about your work in payroll. Then you can ask me anything about Hanse Logistik and the next steps.

questions.text: What draws you to payroll work, and why at Hanse Logistik?
Tell me about a payroll run where something did not add up. How did you find the cause?
How do you handle confidential data and a colleague asking about someone else's pay?
Which payroll systems do you know, and when could you start?

knowledge.text: The Payroll Specialist in Hamburg runs the monthly payroll for about 900 people, answers questions from employees and works with HR and finance.
The payroll team has five people in Hamburg and sits next to the HR service team.
Payroll runs in SAP, with SuccessFactors for employee data. Training on both is part of the first months.
Payroll is mostly on site because of the confidential data. One day a week at home is possible after the first six months.
